narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the breakdown of Amazon's revenue by business segment (Online Store, AWS, Subscriptions, 3rd Party Retail) from 2015 to 2018, establishing the revenue composition before pivoting to a discussion on profitability.

units.meaning: Online Store is the largest revenue segment in each year from 2015 to 2018, with relative values 0.65, 0.57, 0.60, and 0.65.
accepted_routes: Online Store is the biggest segment in every year, with relative values 0.65, 0.57, 0.60, 0.65.
The largest slice is always Online Store from 2015 through 2018.
Online Store dominates the revenue mix, about 0.6 relative value across the period.
units.visual_evidence_rule: In every year of the animation, the encoded mark for Online Store must be visually larger than the marks for 3rd Party Retail, AWS, and Subscriptions.
units.temporal_anchor: Amazon is mostly an online store
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to show Online Store as largest in every individual year, not just overall?

units.meaning: 3rd Party Retail is the second-largest revenue segment in each year from 2015 to 2018, with relative values 0.20, 0.2998, 0.2501, and 0.20.
accepted_routes: 3rd Party Retail is always the second-biggest segment, with relative values 0.20, 0.2998, 0.2501, 0.20.
After Online Store, 3rd Party Retail is the next largest revenue source each year.
3rd Party Retail stays second in the revenue breakdown across 2015-2018.
units.visual_evidence_rule: In each year, the 3rd Party Retail mark must be visually larger than AWS and Subscriptions but smaller than Online Store.
units.reviewer_question: Is 3rd Party Retail's second-place ranking in each year required, or is Online Store dominance sufficient?

units.meaning: Online Store and 3rd Party Retail together make up the large majority of the relative revenue composition, about 0.85 to 0.87 in each year.
units.computation: formula: Online Store relative_value + 3rd Party Retail relative_value by year
accepted_routes: Online Store plus 3rd Party Retail account for about 0.85-0.87 of the revenue mix each year.
The two largest segments together make up the vast majority of relative revenue.
Combined, Online Store and 3rd Party Retail stay around 0.85 relative value from 2015 to 2018.
units.visual_evidence_rule: In each year, the combined encoded area or attribute for Online Store and 3rd Party Retail must be visibly much larger than the combined AWS and Subscriptions portion.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly state that the two largest segments together dominate the composition, or is showing the individual segments enough?

units.meaning: AWS and Subscriptions are the two smaller segments; AWS is consistently around 0.10 relative value, while Subscriptions is smaller, with values 0.05, 0.03, 0.0501, and 0.05.
accepted_routes: AWS is a small segment at about 0.10 relative value each year, and Subscriptions is even smaller.
The two smallest revenue components are AWS and Subscriptions, with AWS consistently above Subscriptions.
AWS stays near 0.10 while Subscriptions stays at or below about 0.05.
units.visual_evidence_rule: In each year, AWS and Subscriptions must be the two smallest encoded marks, with Subscriptions smaller than AWS.
units.temporal_anchor: why we're talking so much about AWS
units.reviewer_question: Should the video call out AWS and Subscriptions as the small revenue components, or only show them in the breakdown?

units.meaning: The segment ordering is stable across 2015-2018: Online Store largest, 3rd Party Retail second, AWS third, and Subscriptions smallest.
units.computation: formula: compare relative_value within each x year to derive ordering; no rank reversal across 2015-2018
accepted_routes: The ranking of segments does not change from 2015 to 2018.
Online Store stays largest and Subscriptions stays smallest across all four years.
The relative revenue mix preserves the same order throughout the period.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The animation must preserve the same rank order of encoded segment marks in every year, with no segment crossing another in rank.
units.reviewer_question: Is the unchanged segment ordering across all four years a required takeaway, or an optional reinforcing observation?

optional_valid: 3rd Party Retail peaks in 2016 at relative value 0.2998, up from 0.20 in 2015 and back to 0.20 in 2018.
Online Store dips to 0.57 in 2016 before returning to 0.60 in 2017 and 0.65 in 2018.
AWS is about twice Subscriptions in 2015, 2017, and 2018 (0.10 vs 0.05, 0.0999 vs 0.0501, 0.10 vs 0.05), but not in 2016 (0.1002 vs 0.03).
Subscriptions has its lowest relative value in 2016 at 0.03.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any absolute revenue dollar amounts, percentages with a % sign, or counts.
Claims about profit, income, margins, or profitability by segment, since the table only has relative revenue composition.
Causal explanations for why AWS is discussed or why segments changed.
Extrapolating beyond 2018 or claiming future growth.
Treating relative_value as a percentage or saying '65%'.
notes: The table only has relative_value 0-1, so all units are relative ranking/composition claims. The narration mentions income/profit, but the table provides no profit data.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
